plugin.name: iki/core
plugin.title: Core
plugin.description: The types every Iki deployment has.

iki/core.Alignment.name: Alignment
iki/core.Alignment.label: Alignment
iki/core.Alignment.description: Sequences aligned, as aligned FASTA, with the ones in Iki linked.

reference.name: reference
reference.label: Reference
reference.description: The sequence the others were aligned to, such as the plasmid a construct should be, or a reference protein.

sample.name: sample
sample.label: Sample
sample.description: The physical material whose reads were aligned.

members.name: members
members.label: Sequences
members.description: The sequences in Iki that it aligns: each is the row headed by its HRID. Rows that aren't sequences in Iki, such as reads, aren't listed.

aligned.name: aligned
aligned.label: Aligned sequences
aligned.description: The alignment as FASTA, a record per row with gaps as - and . where the row has no observation (beyond a read's ends, say): a sequence in Iki is headed by its HRID, or HRID/start-end for part of it, anything else by its own name. The . is Iki's, which other tools reading aligned FASTA take for a residue.

verdict.name: verdict
verdict.label: Verdict
verdict.description: The producing method’s reported agreement with its reference, if it reports one.

method.name: method
method.label: Method
method.description: How it was aligned, such as MAFFT 7.526 (--auto).

iki/core.App.name: App
iki/core.App.label: App
iki/core.App.description: A page of Iki's own components, each panel bound to those before it by expressions.

spec.name: spec
spec.label: Spec
spec.description: Its panels, in order (app/v1). Each is one of Iki's components, or an installed plugin's by its name (`acme/lab.box_map`), with its props and its width on a twelve-column grid. A prop that takes text or an entity can hold expressions between {{ and }}, which read the panels before it by their IDs: an entities grid offers `rows` and `selection`, a viewer `entity`, a plugin's component that lets people pick its `selection`. An app about an entity of a type (`entity.type`) is a tab on their pages in its project, and its expressions read that one as `entity`; a grid's conditions can then hold expressions too.

props.text: {{ size(records.selection) }} of the {{ size(records.rows) }} records shown are picked. Change this app's spec to show what your team needs: a grid of one type, with its own columns; a viewer of the record picked in it; or notes like these.

iki/core.Collection.name: Collection
iki/core.Collection.label: Collection
iki/core.Collection.description: A named set of entities, listed one by one or found by a search.

members.name: members
members.label: Members
members.description: The entities in a static collection, in order.

search.name: search
search.label: Search
search.description: What a dynamic collection holds: a search, as POST /entities/search takes it, without paging. It runs as whoever reads the collection.

iki/core.Complex.name: Complex
iki/core.Complex.label: Complex
iki/core.Complex.description: Molecules held together as one: an antibody's chains, hemoglobin's chains and hemes, a receptor bound to its ligand, or any other complex. It's its parts and how many copies of each, whatever their order, so one set of parts is one registry entry, whichever type of complex registered it.

components.name: components
components.label: Parts
components.description: What it's made of: each part once, with how many copies of it the complex has, and its role in it. An IgG is its heavy chain, two copies, and its light chain, two copies.

part.name: part
part.label: Part
part.description: A molecule it's made of, as its registry entry: a protein, a nucleic acid, a small molecule, or a complex of its own.

copies.name: copies
copies.label: Copies
copies.description: How many of it the complex has.

role.name: role
role.label: Role
role.description: What the part is in it, in lower case, such as heavy, light, antigen or chain_a. A type of complex says which roles its parts may have.
role.pattern_help: lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, such as heavy or chain_a

bonds.name: bonds
bonds.label: Bonds
bonds.description: The covalent bonds between its parts' residues, such as the disulfides between an antibody's chains, or within a part, if they're wanted too. Each names its two residues by their part, which copy of it (from 1), and where they are in its sequence (from 1). A part that's a complex has its own bonds, on it. A registry fact: given once, then changed only by its registrars.

kind.name: kind
kind.label: Kind
kind.description: disulfide two cysteines; isopeptide an amide to a side chain, such as SpyTag's aspartate to SpyCatcher's lysine, or ubiquitin's last glycine to a lysine; thioether a cysteine's sulfur to a carbon; and other anything else, such as sortase A's ligation, a backbone amide from a threonine's carboxyl to an N-terminal glycine.

residue.name: residue
residue.label: Residue
residue.description: Where it is in the part's sequence.

partner_residue.name: partner_residue
partner_residue.label: Partner's residue
partner_residue.description: Where it is in its sequence.

bond_map.name: bond_map
bond_map.label: Its bonds are
bond_map.description: How much of what bonds it its bonds give: complete, every bond it has; incomplete, not all of them, such as an IgG2's between its chains, which take more than one arrangement, so what's worked out with its bonds counts too few; predominant, those of its predominant form, while some of its molecules are bonded otherwise, as a native IgG4's hinge is in some molecules within each heavy chain. Left empty, it isn't said. A registry fact: given once, then changed only by its registrars, as when peptide mapping confirms its disulfides.

molecular_formula.name: molecular_formula
molecular_formula.label: Molecular formula
molecular_formula.description: Its parts' formulas, each times its copies, in Hill order (C, then H, then the rest alphabetically): a protein's from its residues and water, a DNA sequence's from its bases, another part's as its entry gives it, with any isotope it gives written as RDKit writes it ([13C], D for 2H). Each cysteine's thiol free, before its disulfides, and without glycans or any other modification its parts' formulas don't have.

molecular_weight.name: molecular_weight
molecular_weight.label: Molecular weight
molecular_weight.description: Its average mass, from its formula and IUPAC's standard atomic weights (a labelled atom's isotope's mass), each cysteine's thiol free: each disulfide takes 2.016 u off. It's its parts' sequences' or formulas' mass, so a glycoprotein's is its chains' without their glycans.

monoisotopic_mass.name: monoisotopic_mass
monoisotopic_mass.label: Monoisotopic mass
monoisotopic_mass.description: Its mass from each element's most abundant isotope (AME2020), each cysteine's thiol free: each disulfide takes 2.01565 u off.

chain_count.name: chain_count
chain_count.label: Chains
chain_count.description: How many polymer chains it has, counting each copy, its parts' own included: a double-stranded DNA's two strands.

extinction_coefficient_reduced.name: extinction_coefficient_reduced
extinction_coefficient_reduced.label: Extinction coefficient (reduced)
extinction_coefficient_reduced.description: Its molar extinction coefficient at 280 nm (ε280) in water, each cysteine's thiol free (Pace et al., 1995): 5,500 for each tryptophan in its parts and 1,490 for each tyrosine, each times its copies, or a part complex's own. Each disulfide makes a cystine, 125 more. None if a part isn't a protein or a complex with one, as Pace's values weigh only those.

part_disulfides.name: part_disulfides
part_disulfides.label: Its parts' own disulfides, besides its bonds
part_disulfides.description: The disulfides its parts have of their own, each times its copies, and their parts' too: a Fab's four, in a complex of the Fab and its antigen. Its own bonds aren't counted here: an antibody's disulfides are its own bonds between and within its chains, which have none of their own, so it has none here. With its own bonds' disulfides, they're the cystines a lot of it has while its cysteines are oxidized.

part_bonds_complete.name: part_bonds_complete
part_bonds_complete.label: Its parts' bonds counted
part_bonds_complete.description: Whether its parts' disulfides are all counted: false when a part's bonds are said to be incomplete or only its predominant form's, or a part complex's own parts' weren't counted in this project.

iki/core.Organism.name: Organism
iki/core.Organism.label: Organism
iki/core.Organism.description: A taxon, such as a species or a strain, by its NCBI Taxonomy ID: what a sequence, a strain or a sample is from.

taxon_id.name: taxon_id
taxon_id.label: NCBI Taxonomy ID
taxon_id.description: Its ID in the NCBI Taxonomy, such as 9606 for Homo sapiens.

scientific_name.name: scientific_name
scientific_name.label: Scientific name
scientific_name.description: Its scientific name, as the file or database it was first imported from gives it, such as UniProt's Escherichia coli (strain K12) for NCBI's Escherichia coli K-12, until a registrar corrects it. Its NCBI Taxonomy ID, not its name, is what it is.
scientific_name.pattern_help: one line without tabs, starting with a letter, a digit, [ or ', as NCBI writes names, such as Escherichia coli K-12

rank.name: rank
rank.label: Rank
rank.description: Its rank in the NCBI Taxonomy, such as species, strain or genus.
rank.pattern_help: lower-case letters and spaces, such as species or no rank

parent.name: parent
parent.label: Parent
parent.description: The taxon it's in, such as a species' genus, when that's known.

iki/core.Sequence.name: Sequence
iki/core.Sequence.label: Sequence
iki/core.Sequence.description: Anything with a sequence of residues, such as DNA or a protein.

iki/core.View.name: View
iki/core.View.label: View
iki/core.View.description: A saved look at entities in Iki's viewers, each at the revision it showed.

target.name: target
target.label: Target
target.description: The entity it showed, before a view could show several.

target_revision.name: target_revision
target_revision.label: Revision
target_revision.description: The revision of the entity it showed, before a view could show several.

viewer.name: viewer
viewer.label: Viewer
viewer.description: The viewer it showed it in, before a view could show several.

targets.name: targets
targets.label: Entities
targets.description: The entities it shows, in order.

target_revisions.name: target_revisions
target_revisions.label: Revisions
target_revisions.description: The revision of each entity it shows, in the same order.

viewers.name: viewers
viewers.label: Viewers
viewers.description: Which of Iki's viewers shows each entity, in the same order, as the entity's type configures them. Entities in the structure viewer are drawn together, in one Mol* scene; each other one has a viewer of its own.

state.name: state
state.label: State
state.description: What the viewers showed, as they save it. `version` says which shape it is, so older views keep opening. Version 2 has `targets`, one for each entity in order: for the sequence viewer, the feature it showed; for the alignment viewer, the first column and row it showed; for the structure viewer, its colour, whether it's hidden, how it was moved to superpose it on another, and the residues selected. `camera` is where the structure viewer's camera was. Version 1 is a view of one entity, with its `feature`, `camera` or `position`.

transform.description: How it was moved, as a 4×4 matrix in column-major order, as Mol* keeps it.

superposed.description: What it was superposed on (the index of another entity in the structure viewer), and how closely: the RMSD in ångströms over the residues paired.

selection.description: The residues selected, as ranges of each chain's author numbering: from `start` to `end`, each with its insertion code if it has one (`start_insertion`, `end_insertion`), so 35A is a residue of its own, apart from 35 and 35B.
